original_question: Study the first non-integrable point-vortex systems on non-orientable surfaces, and describe the corresponding Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups of those surfaces.
target_in_paper: Section 10.2, Problem 29: "Study the first non-integrable cases for a small number of point vortices on non-orientable surfaces. Describe the full set of Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces, analogous to the ones in the orientable cases."
correct_elements: Your draft already points to the correct official target in the paper: the first non-integrable point-vortex dynamics on non-orientable surfaces, together with Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups. It captures the core content of Problem 29 very closely.
missing_details: The paper explicitly restricts to the first non-integrable cases for a small number of point vortices; the "small number" scope should be retained.
The official statement asks for the full set of Casimirs, not merely some corresponding Casimirs.

In the nearby Hamiltonian context, Casimirs are the metric-independent invariants of the Lie-Poisson structure that specify coadjoint orbits; this meaning is implicit in your draft and should be made explicit for a stand-alone formulation.

The finite-dimensional approximations are approximations for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces, analogous to the orientable-surface constructions discussed immediately before Problem 29; your draft does not state this analogy explicitly.
The nearby sentence identifies representative non-orientable surfaces motivating the problem: the Möbius band, projective plane, and Klein bottle.
The surrounding discussion makes clear that the point-vortex systems are finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems; that context is implicit in your draft.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the missing data are geometric and Hamiltonian rather than algebraic.
refined_question: On non-orientable surfaces such as the Möbius band, projective plane, and Klein bottle, determine the first non-integrable finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems arising from a small number N of point vortices, and describe, for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of such surfaces, the full set of Casimir invariants (that is, the metric-independent Lie-Poisson invariants specifying coadjoint orbits) together with finite-dimensional approximations analogous to those known in the orientable cases.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 10.2, Problem 29, so the correct refinement is to stay with that exact open problem rather than broaden to neighboring questions. I only sharpened it by restoring the paper's scope markers: "small number" of vortices, the non-orientable examples listed immediately before the problem, the requirement of the full set of Casimirs, and the comparison with orientable cases. I also used Section 10.1 to spell out what the paper means by Casimirs in this Hamiltonian setting: metric-independent Lie-Poisson invariants determining coadjoint orbits. I did not expand the target to the separate problems on non-integrability of the full 2D Euler equation or on attractor behavior of integrable vortex cases.
